name: Silver stain (yellow stain)
process: A silver compound (silver nitrate or chloride with a clay or ochre carrier) is brushed on, usually on the back of the piece, and fired at a lower temperature than the paint. Silver ions exchange into the glass surface for its sodium or potassium, are reduced to metal, and grow into nanoparticles; their surface plasmon absorbs blue, so the stain transmits yellow, deepening to amber and orange with more silver or a hotter firing. The stain is inside the glass, not on it: a single piece of white glass can be clear, lemon and amber at once, which is how Morris's quarries have their yellow flowers and the band its figures' hair and haloes.
processSources: G. Molina, S. Murcia, J. Molera, C. Roldan, D. Crespo and T. since.text: Silver stain has been used from about the early 14th century.

nanostructure.text: A layer about 10-20 um thick of metallic silver nanoparticles, from a few to about 100 nm across (Renaissance yellow and dichroic stains).
nanostructure.source: G. Molina, S. Murcia, J. Molera, C. Roldan, D. Crespo and T. Pradell, 'Color and dichroism of silver-stained glasses', Journal of Nanoparticle Research 15(9) (2013) 1932, doi:10.1007/s11051-013-1932-7 (abstract, via OSTI ETDEWEB record 22209451, https://www.osti.gov/etdeweb/biblio/22209451)

colour.text: The colour is set by the particles' surface plasmon absorption and scattering; the same colour is usually seen in reflection and transmission, though some stains are dichroic (yellow and red).
colour.source: G. Molina, S. Murcia, J. Molera, C. Roldan, D. Crespo and T. Pradell, 'Color and dichroism of silver-stained glasses', Journal of Nanoparticle Research 15(9) (2013) 1932, doi:10.1007/s11051-013-1932-7 (abstract, via OSTI ETDEWEB record 22209451, https://www.osti.gov/etdeweb/biblio/22209451)

photograph: Yellow to amber within a clear piece, with soft edges where the stain was brushed; in reflected light the stained area may look slightly milky or different in hue.

unverified.reason: A search summary gave silver-stain firing at 500-650 degC, below grisaille; the primary source was not read.
A silver-nanoparticle plasmon band near 410-430 nm in soda-lime glass was seen only in search summaries.
